name.en: Spare tickets on social media: pay by bank transfer, get nothing

how.en: Someone on social media, often Facebook or Instagram, offers spare tickets for a sold-out gig, festival or football match. They move the chat to WhatsApp and insist on a bank transfer. Once the money is sent, they block you and the tickets never arrive or turn out to be fake. Fake ticket websites work the same way.

text.en: A post or message offers tickets for a sold-out event.
The seller moves the chat to WhatsApp.
They push you to pay quickly by bank transfer.
After you pay, they block you and no tickets arrive.
Can't go anymore so selling my 2 tickets for Saturday at face value. Lots of interest so first to pay gets them. DM me or message me on WhatsApp.

en: bought tickets on facebook never arrived
seller asked for bank transfer for tickets
seller blocked me after paying for tickets
Tickets for a sold-out event from a stranger online.
A move to WhatsApp and a request for a bank transfer.
Pressure that others want the tickets.
Buy only from the venue’s box office, an official ticket site or its official resale service.
Don’t leave the platform’s payment system to pay by bank transfer.
If you paid, call your bank straight away and report it to Report Fraud.
